Page 3
B03-L01 — Analyst semantic model to engineering
dimensional contract
1. Why it matters
A Power BI model can look correct while its physical grain contract is vague. An engineer must make the business process and
one-row meaning explicit enough that a warehouse table can be built and tested from it.
2. What you are learning
Turn familiar star-schema thinking into a business-process + grain contract that controls facts, dimensions and future
implementation.
3. Prerequisite
Course 1 PBM3: you can identify fact/dimension tables, state grain and recognize a star schema. You do not need warehouse
implementation knowledge yet.
4. Picture it in your head
Mental model
Imagine three boxes arriving at a warehouse door: one shipment box, one shipment-event box and one monthly-target box. They cannot be
poured into one container just because they share customer or region labels. Each box has a different “one row means…” sentence.
5. New words before we use them
business process — the real activity being measured, such as shipping a parcel
grain — the exact real-world meaning of one fact row
fact table — rows of measurement/events at one consistent grain
dimension — descriptive context used to group/filter facts
dimensional contract — the written process, grain, keys, roles and rules that implementation must preserve
6. Watch / visual source
Primary visual: Chandoo, Learn Data Modelling & Star Schema for Power BI in 20 minutes, 02:18–09:39. Use it only as a visual refresher. After
watching: close the video and write one sentence each for Shipment, Shipment Event and Monthly Target grain.
Chandoo video | Kimball Grain
Bridge transition
Analyst -> Engineer
What you already know as an analyst: facts hold measurements and dimensions describe them.
What changes in engineering: the model begins with a business process and binding grain sentence before table roles.
Why engineers care: ETL/ELT, keys, tests and downstream totals all depend on that grain.
Small worked example: shipments = one row per shipment; shipment_events = one row per shipment event; monthly_targets = one row per
month-region.
Real engineering version: C3-02 will physically implement these contracts in warehouse/dbt models; B03 stops at a correct
implementation-ready design.
7. Follow with me once
Open Parcel Delivery source_contracts.json and Source_Inventory. For shipments, events and targets, write process + one-row
grain first. Only then choose Fact/Dimension/Bridge roles.
8. What you should see
Three separate fact candidates remain separate. Customers and Services can describe shipment facts. No measure is placed into a
table at an incompatible grain.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B03 Engineering Data Modeling | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 4
B03-L01 — Practice to mastery
9. Why it worked
Declaring grain first prevents “table shape” from making the decision. Facts at different grains can still be analyzed together later
through compatible conformed dimensions.
10. Common beginner mistakes
• Calling every large table a fact without stating its process/grain.
• Mixing shipment revenue with event rows, which repeats revenue.
• Starting from a diagram or Power BI relationship rather than the source process.
• Treating a monthly target as if it were one target per shipment.
11. If stuck
Recovery ladder
Read one file at a time. Say aloud: “one row represents ___.” If you cannot complete that sentence, do not choose the table role yet.
12. Small version alone
Invent a support operation with tickets, ticket status events and monthly team targets. Write three grain sentences and classify
facts/dimensions.
13. Validate
Every fact has exactly one grain sentence. Every proposed measure is valid at that grain. Different grains are in separate facts.
14. Teach it back
Explain in 60–90 seconds why grain is a design contract rather than a Power BI setting.
15. Protected review + changed retry
Attempt protection
After saving your attempt, open Review B03-L01. Close it, then solve the changed support-domain task without copying wording.
16. Evidence / mastery + next route
Ready when
Saved process/grain table + role classification + one rejected mixed-grain design + changed retry + own-words explanation. PASS -> B03-L02;
weak -> targeted grain repair only.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B03 Engineering Data Modeling | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 5
B03-L02 — Key integrity, relationship paths and many-to-many
bridges
1. Why it matters
In analytics, a relationship error may show up as a strange visual. In engineering, a wrong key/cardinality assumption can multiply
rows, lose records, or silently corrupt every downstream metric.
2. What you are learning
Write explicit key/cardinality contracts, distinguish duplicate-key defects from unmatched foreign keys, and use bridge tables only for
real membership relationships.
3. Prerequisite
B03-L01 mastered. From Course 1 PBM4 you already know 1:* relationships and filter direction.
4. Picture it in your head
Mental model
Think of a train station. A dimension key is a named platform that should exist once. Fact rows are passengers with tickets pointing to that platform.
A bridge is a legitimate transfer station for many-to-many membership—not a broom used to sweep duplicate mistakes away.
5. New words before we use them
business key — source-world identifier such as customer_id
foreign key — fact-side value that points to a dimension key
cardinality — how many rows on one side can match rows on the other
fan-out — unexpected row multiplication after a join
bridge table — a separate membership table connecting two many-valued entities at its own grain
6. Watch / visual source
Primary visual: Chandoo 11:50–18:07 for relationship/cardinality/filter flow. After watching: write the Customers→Shipments and
Services→Shipments key contract before opening Power BI.
Chandoo relationship segment | Microsoft many-to-many guidance
Bridge transition
Analyst -> Engineer
What you already know as an analyst: dimension (1) filters fact (*).
What changes in engineering: uniqueness, FK meaning, unmatched-key policy and expected row-count behavior become explicit contracts.
Why engineers care: fan-out and bad keys corrupt data before a dashboard can warn you.
Small worked example: Customer[customer_id] must be unique; Shipment[customer_id] may repeat. Duplicate dimension key blocks the 1-side
contract; unmatched shipment key is separately quantified.
Real engineering version: C3 will add physical constraints/tests and surrogate/history mechanics.
7. Follow with me once
In Parcel Delivery, audit Customers→Shipments and Services→Shipments. Then classify customer_tags at grain customer_id + tag
as a legitimate membership bridge.
8. What you should see
You do not use DISTINCT to “fix” semantic duplication. You can explain why joining Events to Shipments can multiply shipment
revenue.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B03 Engineering Data Modeling | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 6
B03-L02 — Practice to mastery
9. Why it worked
The key contract separates two different problems: duplicate values on the supposed one-side versus foreign keys with no match. A
real bridge represents a real many-to-many business relationship at its own grain.
10. Common beginner mistakes
• Switching to many-to-many because the one-side key is dirty.
• Using DISTINCT after a join without proving which duplicate is semantically wrong.
• Joining two fact tables directly because they share an ID.
• Using bidirectional filtering as a generic repair.
11. If stuck
Recovery ladder
Before drawing any relationship, write four lines: one-side table/key, uniqueness check, many-side FK, unmatched-key policy. If any line is
unknown, investigate source grain.
12. Small version alone
Model Employee↔Skill membership with Employee, Skill and EmployeeSkill bridge. State each grain and composite bridge key.
13. Validate
One-side keys are unique/nonblank where required; bridge grain is real business membership; expected join row-count behavior is
documented.
14. Teach it back
Explain bridge table vs many-to-many shortcut vs DISTINCT cleanup in 60–90 seconds.
15. Protected review + changed retry
Attempt protection
Save attempt -> Review B03-L02 -> close review -> changed Employee/Skill bridge task.
16. Evidence / mastery + next route
Ready when
Key/cardinality contract + fan-out risk note + bridge design + changed retry + explanation. PASS -> B03-L03.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B03 Engineering Data Modeling | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 7
B03-L03 — Multiple grains, date roles and conformed
dimensions
1. Why it matters
A warehouse often contains several business processes at different grains. They must remain separately correct yet still answer
shared questions such as “by date, city or customer.”
2. What you are learning
Keep multiple facts independent, reuse conformed dimensions deliberately, and make role-playing dates explicit without mixing
grains.
3. Prerequisite
B03-L01 and B03-L02 mastered. From C1 PBM5 you know a Date table; this lesson generalizes it across multiple facts.
4. Picture it in your head
Mental model
Picture three transparent maps laid over the same city: deliveries, delivery events and weekly targets. Each map has different dots, but they can
align on shared street/date/city reference layers. Those shared layers are conformed dimensions.
5. New words before we use them
conformed dimension — a shared dimension definition reused consistently across more than one fact
role-playing dimension — one dimension used in different business roles, such as Order Date vs Delivery Date
higher-grain fact — a fact summarized at a broader level, such as week-city target
drill across — aligning separate fact results through shared dimensions rather than joining facts row-by-row
6. Watch / visual source
Recommended visual: Guy in a Cube, Handling Relationships with Multiple Fact Tables in Power BI, 00:00–02:29 and 06:04–08:33. Skip the
middle implementation alternatives for now. After watching: sketch separate facts sharing Date/City dimensions.
Guy in a Cube | Kimball conformed dimensions | Microsoft star schema guidance
Bridge transition
Analyst -> Engineer
What you already know as an analyst: one Date table can support reporting and different relationships.
What changes in engineering: separate fact processes keep their own grain while shared dimension definitions become integration contracts.
Why engineers care: direct fact-to-fact joins create ambiguity and fan-out; conformance lets facts align safely.
Small worked example: Shipment fact uses Booking/Pickup/Delivery date roles; Event fact uses Event Date; Target fact uses Month/Region.
Region/Date can be shared only with compatible definitions.
Real engineering version: C3-02 will implement dimensional tables, keys/history and serving models.
7. Follow with me once
Using Parcel Delivery, draw three independent fact boxes (Shipment, Event, Target). Around them place only dimensions that
legitimately describe each fact. Label Booking/Pickup/Delivery date roles.
8. What you should see
No direct fact-to-fact relationship is required. Targets stay month-region grain. The Date definition is shared but each business role
is named.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B03 Engineering Data Modeling | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 8
B03-L03 — Practice to mastery
9. Why it worked
Conformed dimensions provide common descriptive coordinates. Keeping facts independent preserves their measurements while
still allowing aligned analysis at compatible dimensions.
10. Common beginner mistakes
• Joining facts directly because they share shipment/customer/date columns.
• Expanding higher-grain targets down to transaction rows.
• Using one ambiguous Date relationship for three business dates.
• Calling two similarly named dimensions “conformed” when definitions/domains differ.
11. If stuck
Recovery ladder
Query each fact alone first. Ask: which dimensions are single-valued for one row of this fact? Only then decide what can be shared.
12. Small version alone
Design Orders, Web Events and Weekly Sales Targets sharing Customer/Date/Region only where valid. Name every fact grain and
date role.
13. Validate
Each fact is independently queryable; shared dimensions have compatible definitions; date roles are explicit; no mixed-grain
measure is required.
14. Teach it back
Explain “separate facts + conformed dimensions” to a junior analyst in 60–90 seconds.
15. Protected review + changed retry
Attempt protection
Save attempt -> Review B03-L03 -> close -> changed three-fact e-commerce task.
16. Evidence / mastery + next route
Ready when
Multi-fact diagram + conformed-dimension list + date-role map + rejected direct-fact join + changed retry. PASS -> B03-L04.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B03 Engineering Data Modeling | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 9
B03-L04 — Model reconciliation and engineer handoff
1. Why it matters
A model is not ready for engineering because the diagram is pretty. Another person needs enough evidence to reproduce the
design, test it against raw controls and know which assumptions are still risky.
2. What you are learning
Build an implementation-ready handoff packet with raw-to-model reconciliation, quality policies, ownership, rejected alternatives and
explicit C3 boundaries.
3. Prerequisite
B03-L01-L03 mastered. From C1 PBM6/PBM7 you already know model validation and refresh hygiene.
4. Picture it in your head
Mental model
Imagine handing construction drawings to a builder. A picture of the finished house is not enough. The builder needs dimensions, materials, load
assumptions, checks and what to do when a measurement does not match.
5. New words before we use them
reconciliation — proving important source counts/totals agree with modeled outputs under declared rules
control total — known count/sum/check used to detect silent loss or multiplication
assumption owner — person/team responsible for confirming a business rule
handoff contract — the design/evidence another engineer can implement without guessing
rejected alternative — a plausible design you deliberately did not choose, with the failure/trade-off documented
6. Watch / visual source
Optional visual: Chandoo 20:19–21:32 on why proper modeling matters. After watching: write one failure that a polished dashboard cannot
repair. The lesson/practice packet remains the primary teacher for reconciliation/handoff.
Chandoo closing segment | Kimball dimensional techniques
Bridge transition
Analyst -> Engineer
What you already know as an analyst: validate model row counts, keys, totals and refresh behavior.
What changes in engineering: those checks become a reproducible handoff contract with assumptions, ownership and failure policy.
Why engineers care: downstream implementation cannot rely on “it looked right in my PBIX.”
Small worked example: before trusting Parcel Delivery, reconcile 72 shipments, 216 events, 12 targets, 28 customer-tag memberships and
shipment revenue 26,571.6.
Real engineering version: C3 will convert these controls into automated tests/CI and physical model implementation.
7. Follow with me once
Complete Engineering_Handoff and Reconciliation in the practice workbook. Record source controls before any
relationship-dependent total. Reject one tempting design and name the exact failure.
8. What you should see
Another learner can state every fact grain, key contract, bridge/date roles, raw controls and open assumption without seeing your
Power BI file.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B03 Engineering Data Modeling | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 10
B03-L04 — Practice to mastery
9. Why it worked
Independent controls catch loss/multiplication that visuals can hide. Explicit assumptions separate business uncertainty from
technical correctness and make change safer.
10. Common beginner mistakes
• Using one matching revenue total as proof of the whole model.
• Leaving unmatched keys or data-quality exceptions undocumented.
• Writing “best practice” without naming the failure/trade-off it avoids.
• Handing over screenshots without process/grain/key/control definitions.
11. If stuck
Recovery ladder
Start the handoff as a checklist: process -> grains -> keys -> dimensions -> bridge -> date roles -> relationships -> controls -> assumptions ->
rejected alternative. Fill unknowns honestly.
12. Small version alone
Audit a fresh model sketch that lacks grain/key/control details. Write what the implementer would need before coding.
13. Validate
Raw controls match; fact/dimension/bridge design is reproducible; unresolved quality issues and assumption owners remain visible;
no hidden C3 prerequisite is inserted.
14. Teach it back
Give a 2-minute engineering handoff defense without the lesson/review open.
15. Protected review + changed retry
Attempt protection
Save attempt -> Review B03-L04 -> close -> changed handoff-audit task.
16. Evidence / mastery + next route
Ready when
Completed handoff + reconciliation + assumption owner + rejected alternative + 2-minute defense + changed retry. PASS -> FreshRoute Mini-Lab.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B03 Engineering Data Modeling | INTERNAL QA RC1
Page 11
B03 Quick Reference & Assessment Route
Question
Engineering answer
Business process
Which real activity is being measured?
Grain
What exactly does one fact row mean?
Key contract
Which key is unique on the dimension side; which FK appears in facts?
Bridge
Does this table represent real many-to-many membership at its own grain?
Multiple facts
Do different processes/grains stay in separate fact tables?
Conformance
Which dimension definitions are reused consistently across facts?
Date roles
Which business date does each fact key represent?
Reconciliation
Which independent counts/totals prove no loss or multiplication?
Handoff
Could another engineer implement the model without guessing?
Fresh Mini-Lab
Open B03_FRESHROUTE_MINILAB_DATA_RC1.zip and B03_FRESHROUTE_DIMENSIONAL_MODEL_MINILAB_RC1.xlsx. Solve
independently. The dataset is different from Parcel Delivery and from all Gate domains.
Protected Gate route
Pass all four lessons + FreshRoute Mini-Lab -> Gate A Fleet Maintenance. If Gate A is weak: save attempt -> open Review A -> targeted repair.
Gate B opens only by explicit full-retest assignment; same protection applies to Gate C. Completion percentage cannot bypass the Gate.

quickRevision.text:
C2B / B03
B03 Quick Revision
Grain, key integrity, conformed dimensions and reconciliation
C2B / B03 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT43
Page 1
Closed-book revision map
Lesson
Contract
Engineering rule
B03-L01
Process + grain
Write the one-row meaning before table roles; separate facts at
different grains.
B03-L02
Keys + cardinality
One-side uniqueness and FK meaning are explicit; bridges represent
real memberships, not data defects.
B03-L03
Multiple facts + dates
Use conformed dimensions and explicit date roles; do not flatten
different-grain facts.
B03-L04
Reconcile + handoff
Prove raw-to-model counts/totals and hand off process, grain, keys,
facts, dims, bridges, date roles and controls.
Failure-first recall
- Joining a transaction fact to a lower-grain event/line fact and then summing transaction measures can
multiply those measures.
- A legitimate many-to-many membership belongs in a bridge/factless-fact at its own grain; DISTINCT is
not a semantic repair.
- A monthly or weekly target is a higher-grain fact. It cannot be treated as if the target exists once per
transaction.
- Role-playing dates must stay explicit: booking/order, pickup and delivery dates answer different
questions.
- Reconciliation is a design control, not a dashboard cosmetic. If raw counts/totals cannot be explained,
the handoff is not ready.
Move on when
With the book closed, you can state every fact grain, identify conformed dimensions/bridges/date roles,
predict fan-out before joining and define the reconciliation evidence required before implementation.

masteryCheck.text:
C2B / B03
B03 Practical Mastery Check
Closed-book dimensional-model transfer - non-gating
C2B / B03 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT43
Page 1
Non-gating closed-book mastery check
This check does not unlock, block or replace Gate A. Save a genuine attempt before opening the
protected review.
Scenario - Parcel Delivery
- Using only Practice_Data, classify customers, services, shipments, shipment_events, monthly_targets
and customer_tags as dimensions, facts or bridge/factless-fact candidates. State one-row grain and key
for each.
- Draw or describe the relationship paths. State one-side uniqueness, many-side FK and intended filter
path. Explain why customer_tags is a legitimate membership bridge.
- Explain why shipments and shipment_events must remain separate facts and predict what happens to
booked_revenue if events are raw-joined before aggregation.
- Declare booking_date, pickup_date and delivery_date roles and how a shared Date dimension would
be reused without pretending the three meanings are interchangeable.
- Explain why monthly_targets is a higher-grain fact and how you would compare target vs shipment
actuals at a compatible month-region grain.
- Write a reconciliation checklist: source rows, distinct transaction keys, event coverage, revenue total,
target rows, dimension uniqueness/FK checks and fan-out tests.
- Produce a short implementation handoff and one rejected alternative design with the reason it was
rejected.

C2B / B03 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT43
Page 2
Evidence to save before review
- Process/grain/key/role table.
- Relationship/bridge/date-role sketch.
- Raw controls and a fan-out test.
- Reconciliation checklist with pass/fail evidence.
- Rejected alternative with reason.
- Own-words explanation of what Course 3 will implement later.
Assessment rule
This is mastery evidence only when the model is internally consistent and the raw controls reconcile. A
polished diagram with mixed grain or unexplained fan-out is not a pass.

Changed fresh retry - FreshRoute Mini-Lab
- Close this review and build the same contracts for FreshRoute: 4 cities, 6 restaurants, 10 couriers, 18
courier-skill memberships, 40 deliveries, 120 delivery events and 8 weekly city targets.

delivery fees to 20310.00 if summed at event grain.

conformed-dimension candidate across delivery and target facts.

Ready when you can transfer the grain/key/bridge/date/reconciliation method without the review open
and explain why the rejected flat model fails.

C2B / B03
B03 Engineering Data Modeling
Astra active route - strong teaching preserved - assessment layer deepened
C2B / B03 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT43
Page 1
Open in this order
1) Existing 4-lesson learner book -> 2) matching workbook practice -> 3) Quick Revision -> 4)
non-gating closed-book Practical Mastery Check -> 5) protected review after a saved genuine
attempt -> 6) changed retry -> 7) FreshRoute Mini-Lab -> 8) Gate A.
Why the learner book is preserved
The existing B03 book already teaches the full Astra loop and uses lesson-specific models for grain, key
integrity, conformed dimensions and handoff. RC4 does not replace strong teaching merely to change a
version label.
What RC4 deepens
The weak layer was the one-page Gate reviews and lack of a separate closed-book mastery surface.
RC4 adds Quick Revision, a non-gating mastery check, a protected changed-retry review and deeper
Gate A/B/C diagnostic reviews computed from the real hidden data.
Gate rule
A clean Gate A pass ends B03. Gate B/C remain fresh remediation-only reassessments controlled by
the existing saved-attempt -> protected review -> repair evidence -> changed micro-proof -> explicit
reassignment state machine.
Runtime boundary
Static QA can validate source files, control totals, workbook/package presence, source mappings, PDF
layout and archive integrity. It does not claim learner-machine Power BI, Excel or future warehouse/dbt
runtime behavior.

Use this only after the matching genuine Gate attempt is saved. Diagnose, repair, close the review,
then produce changed evidence. Later Gates remain state-machine protected.
Objective source controls
vehicles 20; technicians 8; work orders 48; part lines 96; labor logs 72; certifications 25
Metric
Protected control
Base service cost

Why a plausible model can still be wrong
- work_orders, work_order_parts and labor_logs are separate grains. A raw three-way join multiplies all
three measures.
- vehicle_certifications is a real membership bridge/factless-fact candidate; five vehicles have more than
one certification.
- Do not repair fan-out with DISTINCT after the join. Fix the model path and aggregate at each fact grain.

C2B / B03 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT43
Page 2
Reasoning and evidence rubric
- State each business process and exact one-row grain before assigning fact/dimension/bridge roles.
- Prove dimension/business-key uniqueness and state foreign-key/cardinality expectations.
- Separate facts at different grains. Predict and test fan-out before any cross-fact aggregation.
- Use bridges only for legitimate membership; never as a broom for duplicate dimension defects.
